ANSWER TO THE USER'S QUESTION FIRST: no, running Fable across this workflow was not on purpose. It is a routing leak. The session model is `fable` (internal/settings/settings.tmpl.json:36 → settings.json:28). The inline script driving this run (projects/-Users-edotau--claude/418826d1-…/workflows/scripts/loop-workflows-understand-design-wf_b5df47de-80b.js) pins only `effort:'high'` on the 4 readers (:27) and 3 proposers (:39). Those leaves therefore inherit the session tier. A per-transcript count of the `"model"` field shows 10 of 13 leaf transcripts ran `claude-fable-5-1`. Of the rest, three judges/critic ran sonnet and the synthesizer ran opus. `usage --workflows` reports 18.7M cache-read tokens for the run but folds the per-model split away.

`claude-code workflow lint` never saw this script, because it only globs `<root>/workflows/*.js` (internal/review/plan/lint.go:33). The six shipped scripts are pinned with two exceptions:
- review-funnel's verifier (review-funnel.js:184-189) is deliberately unpinned with `// lint:opus-ok`, so it also runs on Fable.
- implement-and-verify.js:76 pins opus/high on every run.

Cost fix (Part A, ship first):
- Pin review-funnel's verifier to opus.
- Drop implement-and-verify's implementer to sonnet, with `implModel:'opus'` as an explicit escalation.
- Teach lint to validate pin VALUES and expose a bytes entry point (`plan.LintPins`).
- Add a `workflow-lint` PreToolUse hook on the `Workflow` tool that blocks an inline script with an unpinned `agent()`. The payload field is confirmed from this session's transcript: tool_input carries `script` (inline) or `scriptPath` (resume); a saved-by-name run carries neither and passes through. The hook has the same shape as agent-effort.
The main session itself stays on Fable unless the user changes the template (open question).

Loop evolution (Part B), from the winning recursion-first proposal plus grafts:
1. gate-loop.js gets a separate haiku Detect leaf (graft from minimal-diff/judge 1: detection is its own leaf, not folded into the fixer). Detection order is Makefile → go.mod → pyproject/setup.cfg → package.json → Cargo.toml. The leaf runs only when `args.gate` is absent. The gate fails loudly (status/exit 'error', zero fixers) when nothing is found. The return carries `gate`, `gateSource` and a named `exit` (green|stalled|capped|error). The stall check also covers repeated 'error'.
2. implement-and-verify and audit-fix-verify stop synthesising Go commands and pass `gate: a.gate` through (undefined → detect). The ownership split uses one static TEST_GLOBS list (Go/Python/JS/TS) instead of `*_test.go`.
3. audit-fix-verify recurses on itself via `workflow('audit-fix-verify', {paths: <non-test source files it touched>, round+1, prior})`:
   - It stops with a named exit: dry | stalled (same findings as a prior round, checked BEFORE fixing) | nothing-changed | blocked (gate not green) | capped (rounds, default 2) | error.
   - Files mode becomes multi-language.
   - A null refuter batch goes to `unverified`, not `refuted`.
   - Findings are normalized: package defaults to dirname or '.', and an unknown severity becomes medium with a log line.
4. A new workflows/vendor-leg.js runs one non-Claude leg as a stage. A haiku relay leaf runs `claude-code ask --agent <leg> --format json` with `--timeout ≤3m`, so 3 retry attempts fit inside the Bash tool's 10-minute cap. The script:
   - runs a smoke ask unless `smoke:false`;
   - refuses tasks over 90 KiB (ask caps prompts at 96 KiB);
   - never retries a `--tools` run and never falls back on one;
   - otherwise falls back to a sonnet leaf tagged `fallback:true` (graft from portable).
   audit-fix-verify uses it as an optional second refuter (`refuters:['codex']`, default []): one smoke per round, then one codex call per refute batch in parallel with the sonnet refuter. A finding is refuted if either refutes it with a quoted line. An unhealthy leg is dropped and recorded in `legs`. Gemini/copilot/opencode are not wired into any loop by default (gemini opus tier 429s; sonnet tier is ~20 requests/day). vendor-leg's whenToUse documents one gemini call per round and never the opus tier.

Triggers (Part C):
- CLAUDE.md:75 is the only always-on surface in other repos. It is rewritten from a lookup row into a trigger row that lists every saved workflow. Row 76 mentions the hook.
- agents/claude.md:154/:194 point the manager at implement-and-verify / gate-loop, with codex VERIFY as a leg.
- master-workflow.md Phase 8 and its table are corrected (one gate owner, real args, plus dag and vendor-leg rows).
- orchestrate.md's verify row now routes to gate-loop.
- choosing-a-pattern.md and cross-model-agent-teams.md name the existing scripts.
- The stale "codex hangs" memory-bank line is corrected.

- No shared constants module (SHARED_TREE/TEST_GLOBS are duplicated by hand).
- No rewrite of test-and-fix-fanout or dag.
- No removal of the dead `RANGE || 'HEAD~1..HEAD'` fallbacks (audit-fix-verify.js:140,181,185). They are pre-existing dead code, left alone.
